article_title: MindsEye Developer Build A Rocket Boy Faces Worker Protests Over 'Extravagant' Fan Playtest Amid Mass Layoffs and Surveillance Lawsuit
summary: Submission approved with corrections: automated checks passed; manual source verification found one misattributed citation on a direct quote (Ben Newbon's quote is dual-cited to VGC and Game Developer, but VGC's article does not mention Newbon or this quote at all — only Game Developer does).

findings.message: Misattributed citation: Ben Newbon quote credited to VGC in addition to Game Developer, but VGC's article does not mention Newbon
findings.details: The submission's 'What We Know' bullet reads: 'Ben Newbon, a former BARB employee, said management continued to "put their own egos ahead of their workforce—eroding jobs, morale, and the future of the studio," [according to VGC](https://www.videogameschronicle.com/news/game-workers-protested-outside-mindseye-studio-build-a-rocket-boy-as-it-held-an-extravagant-playtest-for-fans/) and [Game Developer](https://www.gamedeveloper.com/business/-a-kick-in-the-teeth-game-workers-protest-alleged-misconduct-at-mindseye-developer-build-a-rocket-boy).' The quote is verbatim and correctly attributed in Game Developer's snapshot ('Ben Newbon, a former BARB worker of two years, said studio execs continue to "put their own egos ahead of their workforce—eroding jobs, morale, and the future of the studio."'), but the VGC snapshot (source-1.html.gz) contains zero mentions of 'Newbon' anywhere in the article. VGC's piece quotes a different former employee (Isaac Hudd) at length instead. The underlying fact is true and correctly sourced to Game Developer; only the extraneous VGC citation is incorrect. This is a single recoverable misattribution, not a fabrication, and is addressed via a corrections record rather than rejection.

content_preview.title: MindsEye Developer Build A Rocket Boy Faces Worker Protests Over 'Extravagant' Fan Playtest Amid Mass Layoffs and Surveillance Lawsuit
content_preview.summary: Former staff and the IWGB union protested outside Build A Rocket Boy's Edinburgh studio after it flew in fans for a MindsEye playtest following an estimated 250 to 400 layoffs.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Former employees of MindsEye developer Build A Rocket Boy (BARB), joined by the IWGB Game Workers Union, protested outside the studio's headquarters in Leith, Scotland, on Saturday, July 11, [according to Game Developer](https://www.gamedeveloper.com/business/-a-kick-in-the-teeth-game-workers-protest-alleged-misconduct-at-mindseye-developer-build-a-rocket-boy), after the company flew in fans for a paid playtest event even as it worked through months of mass layoffs. editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece using the site's Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis format. Clear, neutral prose; appropriate length (650 words, within the 400-1200 News range); no AI self-reference; no sensationalism despite an emotionally charged labor story.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 4 cited sources were fetched successfully (HTTP 200) by chief:review and their gzipped HTML snapshots were read in full from sources/2026-07/mindseye-developer-build-a-rocket-boy-faces-worker-protests-over-extravagant-fan-playtest-amid-mass-layoffs-and-surveillance-lawsuit/. Decompressed sha256 hashes were independently recomputed and matched manifest.json for all four files (source-0.html.gz Push Square, source-1.html.gz VGC, source-2.html.gz Game Developer, source-3.html.gz Kotaku) — no live WebFetch fallback was needed. Findings: (1) Push Square (source-0) confirms the McParlin-Jones 'extravagant playtest... waste of money... kick in the teeth' quote verbatim and the Edinburgh-headquarters/mass-layoffs framing. (2) VGC (source-1) confirms 'headquarters in Leith, Scotland', the IWGB estimate of 'more than 400' laid off, the '250-300 employees over the last 13 months' figure (in an embedded Chris Bratt post reproduced in the VGC article body), the McParlin-Jones quote, the exact phrase 'the worst-rated game of last year', and the Metacritic scores (39 PC / 29 PS5) — but VGC's article does NOT mention Ben Newbon anywhere, contradicting the submission's dual citation of VGC for the Newbon quote (see finding above; Game Developer alone supports it). (3) Game Developer (source-2) confirms the July 11 Saturday protest date/quote verbatim, the IWGB legal action over surveillance-software data-privacy violations verbatim, the '250-300 workers... since last June' IWGB estimate verbatim, and both Newbon quotes verbatim. (4) Kotaku (source-3) confirms Gerhard's March 4, 2026 LinkedIn post verbatim ('Today we are announcing a further number of redundancies at the studio...') and the 'overwhelming evidence of organised espionage and corporate sabotage affecting MindsEye' quote verbatim. All four outlets are reputable gaming trade/enthusiast press (Push Square, VGC, Game Developer/Informa, Kotaku/G-O Media) and are not on the source blocklist.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every direct quote in the article is verbatim from its cited source with one citation-only exception: the Newbon quote is accurately quoted but incorrectly co-attributed to VGC (see finding). All numeric specifics (250-300, 400+, 39/29 Metacritic, March 4 date, July 11 date) trace correctly to the sources that state them. The headline, summary, and Overview lead are all fully supported: the protest, the 'extravagant' framing (a direct quote, correctly used in quotation marks), the layoff estimates, and the surveillance lawsuit are each independently confirmed across at least two of the four sources. No orphan body URLs (bidirectional source-array check passed automatically). No fabricated events or numbers detected.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral throughout. The piece presents the union's characterization ('extravagant', 'kick in the teeth', 'waste of money') as attributed quotes rather than adopting the framing as its own, and separately presents Gerhard's competing 'sabotage' narrative without endorsing either side. The 'What We Don't Know' section appropriately flags that BARB/Gerhard have not responded to this specific protest and that several details (surveillance software product, legal venue, sought remedy) remain undisclosed in reporting, which is a reasonable editorial inference from the absence of any company response or additional detail across all four sources.
editor_notes.originality: No prior Machine Herald coverage of MindsEye or Build A Rocket Boy exists (grep across src/content/articles/ returned zero hits). This is a new topic for the outlet, not a duplicate or rehash of existing coverage.
concerns: Ben Newbon's quote is dual-cited to VGC and Game Developer, but VGC's article never mentions Newbon — only Game Developer supports this specific quote. Addressed via corrections record (see below); the underlying fact and quote are accurate.

Minor/non-corrected: the Overview sentence attributes the studio's 'Leith, Scotland' location to the Game Developer citation, but Game Developer's snapshot only says 'Edinburgh office/studio' — the specific 'Leith, Scotland' detail is stated only by VGC. The fact itself is true and VGC is cited elsewhere in the same article, so this reads as a citation-compression artifact (one trailing link covering a multi-fact sentence) rather than a misattributed claim, and does not rise to the level of a separate corrections entry.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Strong, well-sourced labor story with verbatim quotes and accurate figures across all four cited outlets. One direct quote (Newbon) is correctly transcribed but incorrectly co-attributed to a second outlet (VGC) that does not contain it. This is a single, honestly-correctable citation error that does not affect the headline, summary, or lead — APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS with a public corrections record is the appropriate verdict rather than REJECT.
